title: Local rings of a smooth algebra over a field are regular
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a smooth $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset A$, the localization $A_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field, line 38609), final assertion, applied at every prime (a globally smooth finite-presentation algebra is finite type and smooth at each prime)

proof.text: Smoothness gives finite presentation and hence finite type. A field is Noetherian, so A is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Its localization A_q is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and local by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

Smoothness includes formal smoothness. Localization preserves formal smoothness: compose its square-zero lifting property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-square-zero-lifting] with that for k -> A. In Lean the instance Algebra.FormallySmooth k (Localization q.primeCompl) supplies this composition. For every square-zero ideal J of a k-algebra D and every k-algebra map A_q -> D/J that kills a positive power of the maximal ideal, FormallySmooth.comp_surjective gives a lift A_q -> D. The power condition need not be used, since formal smoothness lifts every such map. This proves [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] for the maximal-ideal-adic topology.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-field-regular-local] to the Noetherian local k-algebra A_q from step 1 and its adic formal smoothness from step 2. It is a regular local ring. This uses 07EI as a generic tool below the unit level; no realized statement or step of sk-thm-p1 is bypassed.

proof_origin.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07EI, applied after formal smoothness is localized (Algebra, Tag 04EG) and restricted to continuous square-zero test maps (More on Algebra, Tags 07EB and 07NI). Shorter route written by M3.
